reading: The 3x3 input is scaled up x3 into the centre 9x9 of a 15x15 grid (each fg cell becomes a full 3x3 block). Every fg cell on the input's edge also gets a copy of the input placed in the outer ring block next to its scaled block, in each orthogonal outward direction (corner cells get two copies, edge-middle cells one, the centre cell none).

slots.scale: 3 (input size); centre 3x3 blocks of a 5x5 block grid
slots.full_blocks: blocks of input fg cells, filled with the fg colour
slots.copy_anchors: outer-ring blocks orthogonally adjacent (outward) to the scaled block of each edge fg cell

why: every 3x3 output block is empty, solid fg, or an exact copy of the input; solid blocks are the x3 upscale of the input; copies sit only just outside solid edge blocks
invariants: output colours are only bg and the input fg colour

reading: Each 4-shape sits against a straight line of 2; a single marker cell lies on the other side of the line. The shape is reflected across the 2 line and the reflection is drawn in the marker's colour (covering the marker).
verb: reflect across line in marker colour

slots.subject: each 4-coloured object adjacent to a 2 line
slots.colour: the colour of the marker cell on the opposite side of the axis

why: the new cells are the mirror image of the 4-shape about the 2 line, and the marker lies inside that image
invariants: only bg cells (and the marker) change

reading: A full line of 9 runs along one grid edge; the rest is 2-regions and 7-regions with scattered 8 cells. An 8 lying in a 2-region is erased (becomes 2); an 8 lying in a 7-region is duplicated one cell toward the 9 edge.
verb: erase or push marks by region

slots.subject: the 8 cells (marks)
slots.region_colour: the majority 4-neighbour colour around each 8 (2 or 7)
slots.on_7: paint the cell one step toward the 9 border line with 8

why: every output change is either an 8 inside 2 becoming 2, or a new 8 directly adjacent to an 8 inside 7 on the side of the 9 line
invariants: the 9 line, the 2 and 7 regions are unchanged except at 8s

reading: From each 6 on the bottom row a path of 2 is drawn upward; when it meets a horizontal 7 bar it runs along the row beneath the bar (4 at the entry end, 2 along, 3 at the far end), marks the bar cell above the entry with 8, then continues upward past the bar's end, until it leaves the grid (ending with a 6 at the top) or reaches a gap.

slots.source: each 6 cell on the bottom row
slots.path_colour: 2, with 4 / 3 at the turn corners and 8 on the obstacle above the turn

why: the path climbs vertically, sidesteps each 7 bar it would hit by running beneath it to its end, and never crosses a 7
invariants: all 7 cells except one per hit bar stay 7

reading: Four 4 cells mark the corners of a box that contains a partial, scaled-up copy of a small multi-coloured exemplar elsewhere in the grid. The output is the box cut out, with the exemplar scaled to the same factor and completed so it lines up with the partial copy.

slots.crop: box spanned by the four 4 corner markers (corners kept)
slots.unit: the small multi-coloured exemplar outside the box
slots.scale: factor by which the in-box pieces are larger than the exemplar's cells
slots.place: aligned so the scaled exemplar covers the existing in-box pieces

why: output equals the corner box from the input with every exemplar cell drawn as a scale x scale block, consistent with the pieces already inside
invariants: the four 4 corners stay at the output corners

reading: Count the cells of each non-background colour; each count is a perfect square n*n. Draw an n x n square of each colour, sorted from smallest to largest left to right, bottom-aligned, separated by one background column, on a background canvas as tall as the largest square.

slots.items: each non-background colour with its cell count
slots.layout: bottom-aligned, one bg column between squares

why: each square's area equals that colour's cell count in the input

reading: Each solid rectangle contains one odd-coloured mark. The rectangle's interior is cleared to background and diagonals in the mark's colour are drawn from the four interior corners inward until they meet (joined by a straight middle run when the rectangle is not square).

slots.lines: diagonals from the 4 inner corners, in the mark colour, meeting in the middle

why: inside every rectangle, only the outline and the corner diagonals (mark colour) are non-background

reading: The output is 3x3 blocks of the input's size. Each block whose input cell is background gets a copy of the colour-inverted input (fg and bg swapped); blocks of fg cells stay empty.

slots.extent: bg cells of the input (tile extent=bg)
slots.unit: the input with its fg colour and background swapped (not the input itself)

why: every output block is either empty or the inverted input, and it is the inverted input exactly where the input cell is background

reading: The grid is three 3x3 panels separated by columns of 5; only the first panel is filled. The second panel becomes the first rotated 90 degrees clockwise and the third becomes the first rotated 180 degrees.

slots.panels: stripes cut by the 5 separator columns

why: panel k (k = 0,1,2) equals the first panel rotated by k*90 degrees clockwise

reading: The 8-shapes are laid out on a grid of 4x4 squares anchored at the top-left of the fg; every background cell inside a 4x4 square that contains any 8 becomes 2.

slots.blocks: 4x4 squares tiling the grid from the fg bounding box's top-left corner
slots.region: bg cells of every block that contains an 8

why: after filling, every block holding an 8 has no background left and no cell outside such blocks changes (per-object bounding box fails because two blocks touch diagonally in pair 1)
